summary: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. His career included posts at McGill (1960–1964), Yale (1966–1971), and Trinity College and the University of Toronto (1971–1999).

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist who studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University. He served in the U.S. Navy (1942–1945) and held posts at Harvard from 1933, serving as Edgar Pierce Chair from 1948 to 1978.

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He held academic posts as an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and at Heidelberg University (~1976–1993).

Willem Caland was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Leiden University, studying under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Carel Gabriel Cobet. He held posts at Utrecht University from 1903, including Chair of Sanskrit (1906–1929), and Leiden (1913–1914).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and held posts there (~1983–2017) and at the University of Indonesia.

William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and Joe Bransford Wilson. He held posts at Virginia, Dharma Drum Institute, and Chung-Hwa Institute.
William Blackstone studied at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College, Oxford. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Oxford from approximately 1753 to 1766.

William C. Kirby works in sinology and history. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992), Harvard (from 1992), and the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies (~2006–2013).
William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. In 1801, he took up a post as Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College.

William Chittick works in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tehran (~1966–1974) and held posts at Sharif University of Technology, University at Albany, SUNY, and Stony Brook University (from ~1983).

William Dwight Whitney was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Williams College, Yale under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Karl Richard Lepsius, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He spent his career at Yale (1853–1894).

William Edelglass is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held teaching posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of London. He served as president of Shanxi University (1911) and was Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford from 1920.
William Erskine was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the Royal High School and the University of Edinburgh (~1787–1792).
William Evans Hoyle pursued his studies at the University of Manchester from approximately 1874 to 1877 and at Christ Church, Oxford, from approximately 1877 to 1880.

William F. Powell is a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He has held an academic career at the University of California, Santa Barbara, attested from 1986 through 2026 as Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies and Research Professor.
William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered a career in the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

Sinologist William H. Nienhauser, Jr. studied at Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, as well as Bonn. After a post at Indiana, he joined the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1983, becoming Halls-Bascom Professor in 1995.
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge, from approximately 1921 to 1925. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from approximately 1932 to 1969.

William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Harvard, including Harvard Medical School (1864–1869). He spent his academic career at Harvard, serving as lecturer (1872), assistant professor (1876, 1880), and professor (1885).
